Using the scale of 79.0 px/m derived from the ball's gravitational acceleration, the person standing in the middle spans ~145.5 px vertically from feet to top of head in 1280x720 coordinates, corresponding to 184 cm.
When standing upright after kicking the ball (frames 21 to 36), the passer on the left spans ~126 px vertically in 1280x720 coordinates, which converts to 160 cm using the 79.0 px/m scale.
When standing upright (frames 0 to 16), the receiver on the right spans ~144.5 px vertically in 1280x720 coordinates, which converts to 183 cm using the 79.0 px/m scale.

At t=0.00s (frame 0), the horizontal separation between the passer on the left (x~456 px) and the receiver on the right (x~831 px) in 1280x720 coordinates is ~375 px, which corresponds to 4.8 m at 79.0 px/m.

At t=1.00s (0.269s after the apex at t=0.731s), the vertical velocity component is v_y = g * 0.269s = 2.64 m/s and the horizontal velocity component is v_x = 2.08 m/s, giving a total speed of sqrt(2.08^2 + 2.64^2) = 3.36 m/s.
Between t=0.100s (frame 3, x=535 px) and t=1.200s (frame 36, x=715.5 px) in 1280x720 coordinates, the ball moves 180.5 px horizontally in 1.10s (164.1 px/s), which equals 2.08 m/s at 79.0 px/m.
